title: The Small Summer
premise: Sebastian Dravenmoor, grandson of a lighthouse keeper and a novelist whose career is quietly collapsing, returns to the coastal vineyard town of Saltmere for his family's reunion, where his grandmother has promised the estate to whichever grandchild arrives 'whole.' To deflect the interrogation of aunts and exes, Sebastian hires Wren Calloway, the vineyard's new harvest manager, to pose as his partner for the weekend. The fake date curdles into something real over one long summer of rehearsals, storms, and small confidences, until Sebastian must decide whether to accept a publishing rescue that requires moving abroad or stay for the person who finally sees him. He chooses to burn the rescue and stay, signing his next book to Wren on the first morning of harvest.
about_author: Oscar Dunmore is the pen name of a former wine-country line cook who writes love stories set against working landscapes and family obligations. He lives within sight of the sea and insists all his characters deserve dessert.

chapters.title: The Letter with the Wax Seal
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. His grandmother's summons arrives the same week his editor kills his third manuscript, framing the reunion as both family duty and professional humiliation. He almost doesn't go. Emotional beat: dread sharpened into defiance—he'll go, but on his own terms, invisible.

chapters.title: Harvest Manager Wanted
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, new to Saltmere and running from a partnership that ended badly, meets Sebastian when he mistakes her for catering staff at the vineyard office. Sparks of mutual misreading. Emotional beat: two guarded people sizing each other up and liking what they see despite themselves.

chapters.title: A Proposal Over Chardonnay
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Cornered by his sister Marisol about bringing 'someone,' Sebastian impulsively offers Wren a paid weekend gig: pretend to be his boyfriend. Wren, needing rent money before harvest payroll clears, negotiates terms like a contract. Emotional beat: transactional humor masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. They draft the rules—no real names of exes, no touching without cause, exit at dessert Sunday. The comedy of rehearsal: learning each other's coffee orders, childhood scars, tells. Emotional beat: intimacy arriving sideways through preparation.

chapters.title: The Dravenmoor Reunion
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Arrival at the lighthouse-adjacent estate; the gauntlet of aunts, the grandmother's appraising gaze, Marisol's suspicion. Wren plays the role flawlessly—too flawlessly. Emotional beat: Sebastian realizing he's enjoying being seen, which terrifies him.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the reunion dinner, a loaded question about 'when they met' forces Wren to improvise a story so tender it lands on both of them like a confession. Grandmother Dravenmoor's eyes narrow—not with suspicion, but recognition. Emotional beat: the fake becomes a mirror.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A coastal storm strands them past the agreed Sunday exit. Trapped in the lighthouse keeper's cottage, they talk until dawn—about his stalled career, her failed partnership. Emotional beat: the first honest hour; the contract quietly dying.

chapters.title: The Grandmother Knows
chapters.summary: Grandmother Dravenmoor's POV. The matriarch, widowed keeper of both lighthouse and vineyard, privately tells Wren she recognizes a performance because she staged one herself sixty years ago. She offers Wren a choice: keep pretending or earn the truth. Emotional beat: generational echo, quiet menace and grace.

chapters.title: Second Shift
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Harvest season begins in earnest; Wren hires Sebastian for manual labor to keep him close under a plausible pretext. Their hands learn the vines together. Emotional beat: belonging through work, the body believing before the heart admits it.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. His London editor calls: a two-book deal, generous advance, but it requires relocating immediately and a memoir-adjacent tell-all about his family. The career that saved everything once now demands he leave. Emotional beat: hope and trap in the same envelope.

chapters.title: What Wren Saw
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds Sebastian's discarded draft pages and reads the character based on her—flawed, beloved, unfinished. She realizes he's been writing her all summer. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being truly seen, and the fear of what it obligates.

chapters.title: Marisol's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Sebastian's sister confronts Wren: she knows the relationship started as a transaction, and she'll tell their grandmother unless Wren ends it cleanly before the estate is decided. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized; the fake past resurfacing as real threat.

chapters.title: Veraison
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The grapes turn; so does the summer's tone. Sebastian, unaware of Marisol's threat, plans to tell Wren about London over the first ripe cluster. He loses his nerve. Emotional beat: the cost of a withheld truth compounding daily interest.

chapters.title: The Broken Rule
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They break the contract's last clause—no real future talk—and spend a night mapping a life together: the cottage, the harvests, the books. It feels like a promise. Emotional beat: peak happiness, which the reader now knows is load-bearing.

chapters.title: Exposed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the estate's pre-harvest dinner, Marisol reveals the paid arrangement in front of the grandmother and guests. Wren doesn't deny it. Sebastian, humiliated, learns she was threatened and assumes she chose silence over him. Emotional beat: public rupture; both retreat to their old defenses.

chapters.title: The Empty Cottage
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He signs the London deal and packs, telling himself the career is the only thing that never lied to him. He finds Wren's copy of his draft, annotated in the margins with the ending she believes he deserves. Emotional beat: grief curdling into clarity.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Grandmother Dravenmoor's POV. The matriarch shows Sebastian the estate's true condition—mortgaged, failing—and reveals the reunion's 'whole grandchild' test was always about finding someone who'd stay and fight, not someone flawless. Emotional beat: the price of survival named at last.

chapters.title: The Vineyard at Night
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, packing to leave Saltmere before the harvest she built, walks the rows one last time and finds Sebastian waiting where they broke the rule. No speeches—just the question: stay or go, together or not. Emotional beat: the choice stripped to its bones.

chapters.title: Burning the Advance
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian calls his editor and declines the deal, then counters with a different book—the real story of the Dravenmoors and the keeper's light—written from Saltmere. He asks Wren to stay not as a hire but as a partner in the vineyard's rescue. Emotional beat: sacrifice reframed as investment.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Both POVs converging. The whole found family—Marisol repentant, the aunts drafted into labor, the grandmother directing from a lawn chair—brings in the first pick at dawn. Emotional beat: belonging earned through shared work; the vineyard breathing again.

chapters.title: The Dedication Page
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Months later, his new book is accepted on its own terms. At the cottage, he shows Wren the dedication page before anyone else sees it. Emotional beat: quiet, certain love; the writer finally writing the truth.

chapters.title: The Small Summer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. One year on: the vineyard's first successful vintage, the lighthouse relit as a reading room, Sebastian's book on the cottage table. They toast the small summer that turned out to be the whole of their lives. Emotional beat: full-circle peace—survival was never the prize; staying was.
